Sterlite Technologies.why: vertically integrated optical fibre / cable / connectivity maker whose data-center segment rose to 21% of revenue; won a multi-year US$1.1 billion hyperscaler deal for optical connectivity for next-gen AI data centers
Sterlite Technologies.evidence: Sterlite Technologies Q1 FY2027 call (07-24-2026): MD Ankit Agarwal - landmark multi-year $1.1 billion deal with a global hyperscaler to supply optical connectivity products for next gen AI data centers through FY 2029

players.product: Optical fibre (G.654.E, hollow-core, multi-core), high-fiber-count data-center cables (IBR, Celesta) and Neuralis AI data-center connectivity incl. US Conec-certified MMC pre-terminated fiber trunks, array cords and assemblies

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2027 (Group CFO Ajay Jhanjhari): record quarter; revenue INR 1,910 crore, up 87% year-on-year; EBITDA INR 397 crore, up 184%; PAT a record INR 197 crore, 10% of revenue. The data center segment contributed 21% of revenue, up from 1% in FY 2026; North America rose to 54% of revenue from 39% in FY 2026, Europe 25%, rest of world 22%.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue INR 1,910 crore (+87% YoY); EBITDA INR 397 crore (+184%); PAT INR 197 crore; data center 21% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (CFO): having guided a 20% EBITDA margin by the end of FY 2027 and delivered it in Q1, STL revises EBITDA margin guidance upward to 23%; the combined data center and enterprise segment is expected to scale to 50% of revenues in the current fiscal, above the 30% guided on the previous call. No revenue guidance is given. MD: optical connectivity attach rate (16% vs 15% last year) to rise above 20% from next quarter and to 25% by the end of this financial year.
quarterly_data.figure: EBITDA margin guidance 23% (from 20%); DC + enterprise 50% of FY2027 revenue (from 30%); attach rate >20% next quarter, 25% by Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Orders (MD Ankit Agarwal): Q1 order wins of INR 13,100 crores, 1.7 times the INR 7,687 crores won in all of last financial year, anchored by a landmark multi-year $1.1 billion deal with a global hyperscaler (not named) to supply optical connectivity products for next-gen AI data centers through FY 2029, multiple $100 million hyperscaler orders for high-fiber-count IBR cable solutions, and a strategic long-haul order from a major connectivity infrastructure provider.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 orders INR 13,100 crores; hyperscaler deal $1.1 billion through FY 2029; multiple $100 million hyperscaler IBR orders

quarterly_data.signal: Order book (CFO): open order book at a record INR 18,618 crore, up 2.4 times from the last quarter; INR 2,228 crore is slated for execution in Q2 FY2027 and INR 16,390 crore over Q3 FY2027 and beyond (not revenue guidance).
quarterly_data.figure: open order book INR 18,618 crore; INR 2,228 crore for Q2; INR 16,390 crore Q3 and beyond

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (management): capacity utilization (not disclosed) keeps improving quarter on quarter; STL is upgrading equipment and de-bottlenecking across glass, fiber, cable and connectivity, and expects about INR 500 crores of investment per year for the next three years (around INR 1,500 crores cumulative). CFO: STL now has to pick and choose orders based on capacity availability. The $100 million U.S. investment over five years announced in May is mainly a connectivity facility for telecom and data-center customers.
quarterly_data.figure: capex ~INR 500 crores per year for three years (~INR 1,500 crores); U.S. $100 million over five years

quarterly_data.signal: Products (MD): STL achieved US Conec certification of four MMC pre-terminated solutions (about three times the cable density of traditional layouts) under its Neuralis AI data-center portfolio, supported by its South Carolina facility; G.654.E fiber is fully commercialized with 30% lower signal loss, hollow-core fibre cuts latency by up to 47%, and multi-core fibre expands capacity four to seven times, with deployments underway in India and the U.K. STL does not make and is not looking at optical transceivers.
quarterly_data.figure: 4 MMC solutions certified; ~3x cable density; hollow-core latency -47%; multi-core 4-7x capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Raw materials (MD): STL is diversifying germanium sources and expects availability to improve quarter on quarter while developing technologies to cut germanium consumption; helium supply is watched given the Middle East and partly recycled; polyethylene cost increases are largely passed on to customers. CFO: gross margin is under pressure from input costs that rose to significant multiples. Orders are taken keeping raw-material availability in mind.

MD on market and demand: STL's global ex-China optical fibre cable market share rose to 9%; hyperscaler and neocloud capex is multi-year with a backlog of data-center capacity to build (probably 8 to 10 gigawatts in the U.S. this year), and demand 'is outstripping supply currently'. Data-center solutions carry higher margins than telecom. STL secured a definitive victory in its European patent dispute with Fujikura, closing the U.K. litigation on its Celesta cable family.
